download_setup.purpose: Evaluation-only WAV input; no training or generation changes

audio_input.multiple_clips: List of waveforms merged into one multi-audio context
audio_input.timestamp_warning: STTOutput.segments records inference time, not audio time

evaluation_frontend_adjustment.reason: Numerical frontend differences measured before review

method: Every complete WAV is encoded as ordered, bar-aligned <=30s clips in one multimodal request per piece. Official HF Whisper frontend replaces the numerically different MLX native frontend. Labels, MIDI metrics, chords and selection results are withheld from the model.

pieces.prompt:
The audio inputs are consecutive, non-overlapping parts of ONE instrumental performance, in chronological order; concatenate them mentally to assess the whole recording. Audio 1 covers 0.000–27.826 seconds, bars 1–8. Audio 2 covers 27.826–55.652 seconds, bars 9–16. Audio 3 covers 55.652–83.478 seconds, bars 17–24. Audio 4 covers 83.478–113.305 seconds, bars 25–32 and the final release tail.
Review the actual audio, including every supplied part. For each Audio N give one concise observation about audible texture, register, rhythmic regularity, repetition or change, and say if the evidence is uncertain. Then describe: (a) the transition from the first eight bars into the following material; (b) whether later parts develop or remain similar; (c) the ending: a resolved close, a fade, an abrupt stop, or unclear. Do not invent note names, exact chords, exact tempo, composer, title, genre, or quality scores. Do not assume an abrupt change is an error. If an aspect is not reliably audible, say it is unclear. Return JSON with keys clips (list of {audio,observation,confidence}), opening_transition, later_development, ending, uncertainties. Keep the answer under 450 words. You have no MIDI, parameter settings, reference performance, or preferred-version label.

limitations: Audio-language descriptions may be generic or hallucinated and are not listener ratings.
Each audio encoder clip has at most30s context, although all clip embeddings enter one language-model request.
Time and bar coordinates come from verified waveform segmentation, not the backend STTOutput.segments latency field.
Model text is cross-checked with MIDI evidence; model words alone do not verify a chord, a cadence or a preferred configuration.
